correctness.rationale: Using the quoted Definition 3.5, an unselected project p may be outside the cohesive set T, and a voter must reach satisfaction strictly ABOVE µ(T) by adding at most one project. For k>=3,c>=3, set L=min(k,floor c). Singleton private cohesive sets of size L force s+x_i>=L for each i for cardinality EJR-1, and conversely every singleton/common T then meets cardinality EJR-1 if it is not already selected. s=2 leaves no private budget and fails L>=3. s=1 requires x_i>=L−1 and x1+x2<=c and automatically passes cost EJR-1; this occurs at c>=2k−2 and the possible x_i=k−1 or k yield counts 2k²,2k(k+2),2(k+1)² across the threshold steps. s=0 requires x_i>=L, max x_i>c via common-group cost EJR-1, and budget x1+x2<=2c; only floor c=m<k, fractional c−m>=1/2, pairs (m,m+1) or reverse survive, giving 2 C(k,m)C(k,m+1). Both shared projects suffice below c=3 and for k<=2. Independent direct enumeration of budget-feasible outcomes and all cohesive groups T with exact rational costs for k=3,4 corroborates, while proof is exhaustive for all k and real c.

value.rationale: An infinite, naturally parameterized fairness-incompatibility family demonstrates nonmonotone transition: solutions disappear, return in fractional cost windows, and return permanently for sufficiently high cost. An exact labeled-outcome census quantifies how restrictive two simultaneous proportionality notions are, strengthening a known isolated impossibility witness into usable design thresholds.

final_claim: For two voters, two common projects of cost c>0, k unit-cost private projects per voter and budget 2c, simultaneous cost-based and cardinality-based EJR-1 has a complete five-branch exact labeled census when k>=3,c>=3, with recurrent half-integer feasibility windows and high-c recovery; existence holds for 0<c<3 and for k<=2.
limitations: Only two equally entitled voters, two common costly projects, and k symmetric private unit costs.
Exact census only k>=3 and c>=3; below c=3 and for k<=2 only existence stated.
The known k=c=5 incompatibility example is not a new theorem.
